about.hero.title: About Grace & Truth
about.hero.paragraph.1: A Reformed-Baptist seminary (1689 Confession) in Lagos, Nigeria, committed to preparing men and women for faithful ministry.
about.gts_is_a_reformed_baptist_seminary: GTS is a Reformed-Baptist seminary, welcoming applications from anyone who truly desires to be a servant of God.

Holding to the 1689 Baptist Confession of Faith, GTS exists to train men and women for faithful ministry. Through our partner, Grace Bible University (GBU), we offer the Certificate of Ministry, the Associate Degree of Ministry, and the Bachelor's degrees in Theology and Ministry.
Faithful to Scripture. Scripture is held to be the supreme authority in every area of life — the individual, the family, the church, society, and government.
Open to all. Admission is open to both male and female, of any age and any religious persuasion.
Biblically tailored. Our training program is tailored according to the Bible's guidelines for ministry preparation — informing our purpose, curriculum, and faculty.
about.why_gts_exists.heading: Why GTS exists
about.why_gts_exists.paragraph.1: The world is in desperate need of faithful ministers of the gospel — men and women who know the Word of God, love the Lord Jesus Christ, and are able to teach others also. GTS exists to answer that need.
about.why_gts_exists.paragraph.2: Our purpose is to prepare servants of God according to the Bible's own guidelines for ministry preparation. We believe God has given the church a clear pattern for training its leaders, and we seek to follow that pattern faithfully.
about.why_gts_exists.paragraph.3: "Commit these to faithful men who will be able to teach others also." — 2 Timothy 2:2
about.why_gts_exists.what_we_offer.bulle: 1 Theological groundingDoctrine, biblical languages, hermeneutics, and church history.Theological groundingDoctrine, biblical languages, hermeneutics, and church history.
2 Pastoral formationPastoral theology, preaching, and the practical work of ministry.Pastoral formationPastoral theology, preaching, and the practical work of ministry.
3 Personal mentoringA mentoring culture that shapes character as well as knowledge.Personal mentoringA mentoring culture that shapes character as well as knowledge.
4 Recognized credentialsDegrees awarded through our partner, Grace Bible University.Recognized credentialsDegrees awarded through our partner, Grace Bible University.
Our method of preparing men and women is grounded in Scripture itself.
Sound biblical teaching for the mind, so that students know the truth and can defend it. (2 Timothy 3:16–17)
Personal reflection that shapes the heart, cultivating a life of prayer and devotion to Christ. (1 Corinthians 2:6–16)
Faithful training under godly mentors, preparing students to entrust the Word to the next generation. (2 Timothy 2:2; Matthew 28:19–20)
about.a_christian_theistic_world_and_lif: GTS adopts the philosophy of education of Grace Bible University, which is based upon a Christian theistic world-and-life view — an inclusive philosophy of life that derives consistently from the Scriptures.

This is the first and overshadowing presupposition for a truly biblical approach to education. There is no higher authority for man in knowledge and reasoning. God is absolute, and his revelation comes to man with absolute authority; it is the inspired, infallible, inerrant, and all-sufficient Word of God.
Scripture is held to be the supreme authority in every area of life for the individual, the family, the church, society, and government.
Education is not merely the transfer of information; it is the formation of a whole person whose thinking and living are brought into line with the truth of God.
Our philosophy touches every course we teach and every relationship we build — because the Christian worldview is an inclusive philosophy of life.
about.the_1689_baptist_confession.paragr: GTS is a Reformed-Baptist seminary that holds faithfully to the Second London Baptist Confession of Faith (1689).
about.the_1689_baptist_confession.reform: Committed to the historic Reformed doctrines of grace — God's sovereignty in salvation and his glory in all things.
about.the_1689_baptist_confession.baptis: Convicted of believers' baptism and the congregational government of the local church according to Scripture.
about.the_1689_baptist_confession.confes: Standing in the stream of historic Baptist confessional theology, teaching what faithful Baptists have believed for centuries.
about.the_men_god_has_given_to_gts.headi: The men God has given to GTS
about.the_men_god_has_given_to_gts.parag: An academic environment shaped by godly mentors who combine expertise and passion for the glory of God.
Additional assisting and visiting part-time lecturers serve alongside the core faculty. Portraits to be added.

academics.hero.title: Academics
academics.hero.paragraph.1: From the Certificate of Ministry to the Bachelor's degrees, our curriculum follows a clear progression — and the credits of each degree can be applied toward the next higher degree.
academics.four_programs_one_faithful_fou: All programs follow the study methodology of Grace Bible University, tailored according to the Bible's guidelines for ministry preparation.
A one-year program for those beginning the call to ministry. Students gain a solid introduction to the Scriptures, doctrine, and church history.
Church history and the sovereignty of God
Credits apply toward the Associate Degree
Two years of deeper biblical grounding and pastoral formation, building on the Certificate and preparing students for service in the local church.
Church history and the life of Christ
Credits apply toward the Bachelor's degree
A four-year degree for rigorous theological study — biblical languages, hermeneutics, apologetics, and the history of the church — preparing teachers and theologians.
Differs from the B.Min only in the final year
A four-year degree centered on pastoral practice — preaching, pastoral theology, and the practical work of shepherding God's people.
Differs from the B.Th only in the final year
All courses are 3 units each. The Bachelor of Theology differs from the Bachelor of Ministry only in the final year of study.

academics.how_gts_students_study.heading: How GTS students study
academics.how_gts_students_study.paragra: GTS has fully adopted the study methodology of GBU, which has developed a unique method of study.
academics.how_gts_students_study.reflect: This part of the course is designed to let the student interact with the mentor on a one-to-one basis. While there is much freedom to respond, all responses should ultimately end within the framework of a Christian worldview and be defended by the Word of God. If, upon discussion, the mentor finds that a student's answer needs to be more biblically based, he will have the student either rewrite or add to a portion of their response.
academics.how_gts_students_study.scriptu: The student is expected to memorise and recite, without help, the passages of Scripture indicated, in order to complete the individual course. Chapter and verse must be included in the memorisation response.
academics.how_gts_students_study.persona: Practical suggestions are offered on how the material studied can be applied in life. Questions and answers are based upon the text — there will be no answer that cannot be easily found within the material. Each student is encouraged to use a complete sentence when responding, so as to learn to think clearly and logically.
academics.how_gts_students_study.self_as: This is a private and personal assessment of one's own heart. It does not need to be shared or discussed.
"Examine yourselves as to whether you are in the faith. Test yourselves. Do you not know yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you — unless indeed you are disqualified?" — 2 Cor. 13:5
Course Descriptions
A sample of what you'll study
Biblical Studies
PBIB 101 · How to Study the Bible. A work by R. A. Torrey designed to help the student learn the major concepts and principles of Bible study. (3 semester units)
BIB 102 · Introduction to the Scriptures. Utilizes W. Graham Scroggie's classic Know Your Bible, providing a brief introduction to all the books of the Bible. (3 semester units)Know Your Bible

BIB 201 · Biblical Hermeneutics I. A study of the issues, history, and principles of biblical interpretation, using Dr. W. R. Downing's An Introduction to Biblical Hermeneutics, Part I. (3 semester units)An Introduction to Biblical Hermeneutics
BIB 202 · Biblical Hermeneutics II. Continues the study of interpretation using Part II of Downing's hermeneutics text. (3 semester units)
Survey & Languages
BIB 203 · Old Testament Survey I. Genesis through the Song of Solomon, with introduction, analysis, and practical observations for each book (Downing). (3 semester units)
BIB 204 · Old Testament Survey II. Isaiah through the intertestamental era, with introduction, analysis, and practical observations. (3 semester units)
BIB 205 · New Testament Survey I. Matthew through Acts. (3 semester units)
BIB 206 · New Testament Survey II. The life and epistles of the Apostle Paul. (3 semester units)
BIB 301 · New Testament Survey III. The General Epistles and Revelation. (3 semester units)
Elementary Greek & Elementary Hebrew. Foundational study of the biblical languages. (3 semester units each)
Revival & Missionary Studies
History of Revival. A study of God's reviving work in the church across the centuries.
The Life of George Müller. The testimony of a man of faith — prayer, providence, and practical trust in God.
New Testament Missionary. The pattern of missions in the New Testament church.
Exposition & Pastoral Theology
New Testament Exposition. The discipline of faithfully explaining and applying the Word of God.
Pastoral Theology. The work of the pastor — shepherding, teaching, and leading the local church.
Theology of Prayer. The biblical foundation and practice of prayer.

faq.hero.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.hero.paragraph.1: Answers to the questions students most often ask about GTS — what we are, when to apply, the CBTS master's program, and more.
faq.about_gts.heading: About GTS
faq.about_gts.question.1: What is Grace & Truth Theological Seminary (GTS)?
faq.about_gts.paragraph.1: GTS is a Reformed-Baptist seminary holding to the 1689 Baptist Confession of Faith. It is a ministry of Sovereign Grace Bible Church, Lagos, and is affiliated with Grace Bible University (USA).
faq.about_gts.paragraph.2: We welcome applications from anyone who truly desires to be a servant of God. Through our partner GBU, GTS offers the Certificate of Ministry, the Associate Degree of Ministry, and the Bachelor's degrees in Theology and Ministry.
faq.about_gts.paragraph.3: GTS stands in the historic Baptist tradition, affirming the Reformed doctrines of grace as summarized in the Second London Baptist Confession of Faith (1689). This shapes our theology, our philosophy of education, and everything we teach.
faq.about_gts.paragraph.4: Admission is open to both male and female students, of any age and of any religious persuasion. If you truly desire to be a servant of God, we welcome your application.
faq.about_gts.question.4: What is the relationship between GTS and Grace Bible University (GBU)?
faq.about_gts.paragraph.5: GTS is affiliated with Grace Bible University (USA), through whom our certificates and degrees are awarded upon completion of course requirements. GTS has fully adopted GBU's unique study methodology, combining doctrine, meditation, and mentoring.
faq.programs_academics.heading: Programs & Academics
faq.programs_academics.paragraph.1: GTS offers four programs through Grace Bible University:
faq.programs_academics.bullet.2: Associate Degree of Ministry — 2 years, 60 units
faq.programs_academics.bullet.3: Bachelor's Degree of Theology — 4 years, 120 units
faq.programs_academics.bullet.4: Bachelor's Degree of Ministry — 4 years, 120 units
faq.programs_academics.paragraph.2: The credits of each degree can be applied toward the next higher degree.
faq.programs_academics.question.2: Do you offer a master's program? What about the CBTS master's program?
faq.programs_academics.paragraph.3: Yes. Beyond our certificate and bachelor's programs, GTS connects students with master's-level study through our partnership with Covenant Baptist Theological Seminary (CBTS) — a Reformed Baptist seminary offering graduate programs including the Master of Arts (M.A.) in fields such as Pastoral Studies, Biblical Studies, and Reformed Baptist Studies, the Master of Divinity (M.Div.), and the Master of Theology (Th.M.).
faq.programs_academics.paragraph.4: CBTS is designed for students preparing for faithful, church-centered ministry in the Reformed Baptist tradition, and its courses can be taken by students anywhere — with live-streamed and self-paced options.
faq.programs_academics.paragraph.5: Details on CBTS admission requirements and how GTS students apply will be added here. Contact the seminary for the current pathway.
faq.programs_academics.question.3: What is the study method at GTS?
faq.programs_academics.paragraph.6: GTS has fully adopted the study methodology of GBU. Each course uses a Student's Study Guide workbook, and students engage through four elements:
faq.programs_academics.bullet.5: Reflection & Discussion — one-to-one interaction with a mentor, grounded in a Christian worldview
faq.programs_academics.bullet.6: Scriptural Memory Work — memorising and reciting the passages of Scripture for each course
faq.programs_academics.bullet.7: Personal Application — practical application of the material to life
faq.programs_academics.bullet.8: Self-Assessment — a private examination of one's own heart (2 Cor. 13:5)
faq.programs_academics.question.4: How long does each program take?
faq.programs_academics.paragraph.7: The Certificate of Ministry is a 1-year program (30 units), the Associate Degree of Ministry is a 2-year program (60 units), and each Bachelor's degree is a 4-year program (120 units). Because credits roll forward, a student can progress from the Certificate to a Bachelor's along one seamless pathway.
faq.admission_application.heading: Admission & Application
faq.admission_application.question.1: When can students apply to GTS?
faq.admission_application.paragraph.1: Applications open ahead of each academic year. For the 2026 academic year, applications open in February and the deadline is 30 March 2026, followed by board interviews and admission letters in April. Check the important dates page for the current calendar, or contact the seminary for exact deadlines.
faq.admission_application.bullet.1: Completion of secondary school or an equivalent educational level (the applicant must be able to read and write).
faq.admission_application.bullet.2: Duly filled registration forms submitted accordingly.
faq.admission_application.bullet.3: A letter of recommendation from a church officer approving the student's desire to study at GTS.
faq.admission_application.bullet.4: Two references providing full name, profession, designation, home or office address, email, phone number, and relationship to the applicant.
faq.admission_application.paragraph.2: Complete the registration forms, submit them with your two references and your letter of recommendation. Your application will be evaluated, and an interview will be conducted by one or more members of the board of GTS. All admitted students are contacted, and their names are published on the GTS website.
faq.admission_application.question.4: Do I need a letter of recommendation?
faq.admission_application.paragraph.3: Yes. A letter of recommendation from a church officer approving the student's desire to study at GTS is required. Exceptions may be considered on a case-by-case basis by the board of the seminary.
faq.admission_application.question.5: Can I study at GTS if I am not a Baptist?
faq.admission_application.paragraph.4: Admission is open to students of any religious persuasion. GTS teaches faithfully within the Reformed-Baptist tradition, and welcomes applications from anyone who truly desires to be a servant of God.
faq.fees_costs.heading: Fees & Costs
faq.fees_costs.paragraph.1: Yes. GTS is committed to removing financial barriers to faithful preparation, and our seminary training is offered free of tuition. Please contact the seminary regarding any registration or material fees that may apply.

resources.a_library_for_faithful_study.p: Students at GTS are encouraged to build the habit of wide, careful reading. Here we point to the classic works of Reformed and Baptist theology that have served the church for centuries.
resources.a_library_for_faithful_study.b: The Baptist Confession of Faith (1689) — the doctrinal standard of the seminary.
Confessions and catechisms of the Reformed tradition, for families and churches.
Expository and systematic theologies recommended by our faculty.
A selection of biographies, including the life of George Müller, for encouragement in faith.
resources.a_library_for_faithful_study.p: "Faith comes by hearing, and hearing by the word of God."
